author: Codex, with no independent external annotator
selection: Source-page-first purposive selection of legible new named locations covering all eight districts; selected from actual PDF rows, not system predictions. Four existing core sources; place-disjoint, not source-disjoint. No engine/scorer changes or trial holdout inference during authoring.

insufficient_evidence_rationales.HQ18: The frozen sources cannot establish a site measurement on 2 October 2026; H001 is a report value, not that dated observation.
insufficient_evidence_rationales.HQ19: Table 4 gives counts and exceedance percentages, not sample concentrations or their arithmetic mean.
insufficient_evidence_rationales.HQ20: Annexure V gives basic chemical parameters including fluoride but has no arsenic column. Scope is explicitly this annexure; no global absence claim.

not_comparable_rationales.HQ13: Different locations and source types; no established time ordering or repeated-well identity.
not_comparable_rationales.HQ14: Samples and habitations are different counting entities.
not_comparable_rationales.HQ15: Different locations sampled in the same stated period, not a before/after pair.
not_comparable_rationales.HQ16: Distinct TW and DW well IDs; same sampling date does not make them repeated measurements of one well.
not_comparable_rationales.HQ17: Different locations and aquifer/source classes in the same period cannot establish a temporal decline.

limitations: Convenience sample, not randomized or source-disjoint.
Same assistant implemented fixes and authored holdout; not independently blind. Prior conversation contained original benchmark material.
Numeric questions name source/annexure and many share a template; tests precise lookup more than open-ended search.
Comparison and abstention tasks have explicit scope and are not a representative user sample.
Existing scorer only checks comparison answer type and numeric value/page, not the full semantic tuple; PDF verification is separate.
No source page used here is image-only; all provide extractable text.
